chapter: Glen Island, early records and Duke Ellington
title: Adrian Rollini on bass sax and vibraphone
summary: Barnet recalls recording dates with Adrian Rollini, including California Ramblers sessions, and using him on vibraphone.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, I've seen them. I know Harry Carney used to admire a bass sax. Who was it, Adrian Rollini --
He used to talk about a lot, and how much he admired him.

Yes, Adrian did a date under the name of the California Ramblers, and I think -- was it that one, or -- no, it was one of those Brunswick dates, and that I did with him. That's right, I worked with him. It was one of those groups. It was he and I and Arthur Schutt and Jimmy Dorsey playing clarinet and if I'm not mistaken, Manny Klein. You'd just go in and play the popular tunes of the day, and -- and then I used him on vibraphones on one date that I did for the Irving Mills thing. I think that was a California Ramblers date, too. Or it could have been mine.
I didn't know he played vibraphone.
Oh, I didn't know that. I only knew about the bass sax.
